boards.school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
boards.title: Your First Weekend at Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College, Shared as Ca
boards.description: An under-21-safe Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning LSU’s central landmarks, recreation options, gathering spaces, and ways to find future campus activities.

cards.title: Start at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday evening orientation stop
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, scan the building directory, and identify a comfortable meeting point before exploring farther.
cards.short_summary: Learn the practical center of campus before the weekend gets underway.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies a second-floor information desk for questions about the Student Union and campus; normal Friday building hours extend to 10 p.m. during fall and spring semesters.
cards.access_notes: Normal fall and spring hours are Friday 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; reduced interim, holiday, closure, and event schedules may apply.

cards.title: Build a Weekend Shortlist
cards.subtitle: Friday event-planning check
cards.notes: Create your TigerLink profile, filter the current listings by interest, and save one future organization or campus event.
cards.short_summary: Turn a quiet first evening into a plan for meeting people later.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes TigerLink as its platform for discovering student organizations and events, registering for activities, and tracking involvement.
cards.access_notes: TigerLink is an online platform; individual events may require registration, LSU credentials, or separate eligibility checks.

cards.title: Cross the Historic Quad
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning campus bearings
cards.notes: Walk the main paths, note the surrounding academic buildings, and choose an easy landmark for future meetups.
cards.short_summary: Use LSU’s historic core to establish a mental map of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the Quadrangle as the historic core of campus, completed before the 1926 dedication and used as a main walking thoroughfare.
cards.source_title: The Quad at LSU: The Heart of Campus, both Lush and Inviting
cards.access_notes: Remain on established pedestrian routes and observe temporary restrictions or university notices affecting outdoor areas.

cards.title: Read the Mounds’ Story
cards.subtitle: Saturday respectful history stop
cards.notes: Study the interpretive panels from outside the protected area, then leave the fragile earthworks completely undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: Encounter the site’s Indigenous history while following its preservation rules.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU says the Campus Mounds are publicly accessible historic earthworks, but visitors must admire them from a safe distance and may not walk, sit, or slide on them.
cards.source_title: LSU Campus Mounds | A Native American Mounds Historical Site
cards.access_notes: View from a safe distance, obey posted rules and protective barriers, and never climb, sit, slide, or bicycle on the mounds.

cards.title: Pause for the Alma Mater Chimes
cards.subtitle: Saturday noon landmark stop
cards.notes: Reach the tower plaza before noon, view the World War I memorial exterior, and listen for the scheduled alma mater chime.
cards.short_summary: Connect a recognizable campus landmark with its memorial purpose.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that Memorial Tower honors Louisianans who died during World War I and that the tower chimes the LSU Alma Mater at noon.
cards.access_notes: The noon chime is documented by LSU; this stop is framed around the exterior plaza, not assumed museum entry.

cards.title: Visit Mike’s Habitat
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon mascot stop
cards.notes: Read the tiger-conservation displays, observe quietly from the public viewing area, and accept that Mike may be indoors.
cards.short_summary: Meet LSU’s live mascot through a welfare-conscious public visit.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU locates the Tiger Habitat on North Stadium Drive, states there is no fee to visit, and says Mike is usually outside daily between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m., with times varying.
cards.access_notes: Mike is usually outside 8 a.m.–7 p.m., including weekends, but availability varies for animal care, maintenance, and yard work.

cards.title: Reserve a Tiger Stadium Tour
cards.subtitle: Saturday book-ahead campus landmark
cards.notes: Check the official calendar first, buy a timed ticket at least a day ahead, and arrive at the Bill Lawton Room as directed.
cards.short_summary: See the stadium interior through an authorized guided visit.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics offers approximately 45-minute guided Tiger Stadium tours on select dates, with advance ticket purchase required at least 24 hours before the scheduled start.
cards.access_notes: Tours operate only on listed dates, require tickets at least 24 hours ahead, and begin at the Bill Lawton Room; the route may change.

cards.title: Try the Climbing Area
cards.subtitle: Saturday active campus stop
cards.notes: Check the live schedule and eligibility, wear closed-toe shoes, then ask staff about orientation before attempting a route.
cards.short_summary: Sample campus recreation while learning the facility’s safety process.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU UREC documents a climbing area with top-rope and bouldering walls and requires participants to check in, follow equipment rules, and pass testing before belaying.
cards.access_notes: Verify current open-climb hours and entry eligibility; check in at the desk, wear closed-toe shoes, and follow all posted climbing policies.

cards.title: Loop Part of University Lake
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning outdoor reset
cards.notes: Choose a manageable out-and-back walk, stay aware of cyclists and uneven edges, and turn back before heat or fatigue builds.
cards.short_summary: Begin Sunday with an adaptable lakeside walk close to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Campus Life explicitly recommends walking, running, riding, or skating the University Lakes as an LSU activity.
cards.source_title: 101 Things to Do at LSU | LSU Campus Life
cards.access_notes: Use established public routes, account for weather and ongoing restoration conditions, and follow all posted detours or safety notices.

cards.title: Finish on the Parade Ground
cards.subtitle: Sunday route-recap stop
cards.notes: Face the surrounding landmarks, retrace the weekend route on your phone, and save two dependable meeting points for later.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend by connecting its stops into one usable campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the Parade Ground as a named central campus green used for university gatherings, including the recurring Fall Fest tradition.
cards.access_notes: The open lawn may be reserved or restricted for scheduled events; observe posted notices and avoid organized sports or cleats.

warnings: Tiger Stadium tours require advance purchase and are offered only on select dates.
UREC access, eligibility, reservations, and activity hours should be checked immediately before visiting.
Outdoor stops may be affected by weather, university events, construction, or game-day controls.
